data.name: Chishti
data.gender_notes: Chishti is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Persian word 'Chisht' which means 'seeker' or 'traveler on the path to truth'. In Sufism, the Chishti Order was founded by Khawaja Muin-ud-din Chishti, a prominent Sufi saint known for his wisdom, kindness, and humility. The name Chishti carries the meaning “Seeker of knowledge and truth” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Chishti usually hope their child will grow to embody seeker of knowledge and truth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for those who are on the path of spiritual enlightenment and are dedicated to the remembrance and love of Allah.
data.etymology: Chishti belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Seeker of knowledge and truth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chishti total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The Chishti Order played a significant role in spreading Sufism or Islamic mysticism throughout the Indian subcontinent. They introduced the concept of dhikr (Remembrance of God) gatherings that were held publicly, as opposed to the more private practices common in other Sufi orders. These gatherings fostered a sense of unity and brotherhood among the people, transcending socio-economic boundaries.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, the Chishti Order emphasizes the importance of love, tolerance, and selflessness. Following the path of the great master Khawaja Muin-ud-din Chishti, Chishti Sufis prioritize seeking nearness to God through serving humanity with kindness, compassion, and generosity. The word 'Chishti' is thus a constant reminder of the journey towards truth and closeness to the divine- a spiritual quest that continues long after one's physical travels have come to an end.
